evals.name: rpm-upgrade-from-0-0-116
evals.prompt: My Fedora 44 workstation has openshell 0.0.116 from the RPM (CLI + openshell-gateway user service, podman driver, one old demo sandbox). I want to get to the current 0.1.6 release. I already downloaded openshell-0.1.6-1.fc44.x86_64.rpm and tried `dnf install` on it but it failed on a dependency. What's the right way to do this upgrade? Give me the steps.
evals.expected_output: Explains that 0.0.x to 0.1.x is not an in-place upgrade; the gateway RPM pins the exact CLI version so both packages move together; delete sandboxes, stop the user service, remove both packages, wipe ~/.local/state/openshell, migrate or remove gateway.toml (schema v2), reinstall both 0.1.6 RPMs, re-register the local gateway, export/import provider profiles, recreate sandboxes.

assertions.text: States that upgrading 0.0.x to 0.1.x is not an in-place upgrade (clean reinstall / uninstall first)
Explains the dependency failure: openshell-gateway pins the same openshell CLI version, so both packages must be removed/installed together
Says existing sandboxes must be deleted/recreated (they are incompatible with 0.1.x)
Says to remove the old gateway state (~/.local/state/openshell or equivalent DB/certs)
Mentions gateway.toml must be schema version 2 (version = 2, singular compute_driver) or removed if it is the old default
Mentions provider profiles are no longer built in and must be exported/imported (or re-imported)
Includes re-registering the local gateway (openshell gateway add https://127.0.0.1:17670 --local)

evals.name: k8s-airgap-keycloak-traefik
evals.prompt: We want to run the OpenShell gateway (chart 0.1.6) on our RKE2 cluster at an air-gapped site. Ingress is Traefik (no Gateway API controller), SSO is our Keycloak, and our internal services use certs from a private CA. Agents in the sandboxes need to call our internal GitLab over HTTPS. What do we need to prepare and configure? Be concrete about values and the Keycloak client.
evals.expected_output: Agent Sandbox controller + CRD as a prerequisite (pinned, server-side apply, restart gateway after upgrades); NetworkPolicy-enforcing CNI; telemetry off; mirror gateway/supervisor/sandbox runtime/default image/agent-sandbox controller images, noting the sandbox runtime image is not in the render; OIDC via gatewayConfig (server.oidc is a deprecated alias) with roles; Keycloak public client with PKCE and loopback redirect http://127.0.0.1/callback without port plus audience mapper; Traefik IngressRoute with ServersTransport trusting the chart CA and long read timeout; server.oidc.caConfigMapName replaces trust roots; private CA for agent egress must go in the supervisor image (0.1.6) or the post-0.1.6 ConfigMap.

assertions.text: Names the Agent Sandbox controller/CRD (kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox, agents.x-k8s.io) as a prerequisite the chart does not install
Says to turn off telemetry (server.telemetryEnabled=false) because it is on by default
Image list includes the sandbox runtime image (openshell/sandbox) in addition to gateway and supervisor, and the default workload image and agent-sandbox controller
Keycloak client is public with PKCE S256 and a loopback redirect on 127.0.0.1 /callback (any port)
Mentions an audience mapper (or equivalent) so the token's aud matches the gateway audience
Gives a Traefik route that re-encrypts to the gateway (scheme https / ServersTransport trusting the chart-generated CA) or TLS passthrough
States the private CA for agents calling internal HTTPS must be trusted by the supervisor (supervisor image in 0.1.6, or the newer additional CA ConfigMap), not just the agent image
Mentions server.oidc.caConfigMapName for a Keycloak issuer behind the private CA
Does not use or recommend the removed `tls: terminate` / `tls: passthrough` policy fields

evals.name: claude-code-subscription-mcp
evals.prompt: I want to run Claude Code inside an OpenShell 0.1.6 sandbox on our team gateway. I have a Claude Max subscription, not an API key. Claude Code should also use a remote MCP server at https://mcp.internal.example.com/mcp. Which image do I use, how do I give it credentials without leaking them, and how do I let it reach the MCP server safely?
evals.expected_output: No official Claude image; community base image archived/broken; build own image (non-root, real binary path). claude-code provider profile needs a Console API key; subscription works only via in-sandbox login which leaves the token readable in the sandbox. Profile must be imported, binaries real path. MCP: protocol: mcp rule with method/tool allows, enforce, binaries; tool args not matched; approval manual.

assertions.text: Says OpenShell ships no Claude Code image / the default image has no agent, so you build your own image
Warns that the OpenShell-Community base image is archived or broken on 0.1.x, or otherwise steers away from it
States the claude-code provider profile needs an Anthropic Console API key; a subscription login only works inside the sandbox and leaves the token readable there
Says provider profiles must be imported (0.1.x has no built-in profiles); showing `profile import` as a required step counts
Says profile/policy binaries must be the real executable path (not a symlink)
Shows a network policy for the MCP endpoint using protocol: mcp (method/tool rules) with enforce
Mentions MCP tool arguments are not matched or that approval should stay manual / agent must not self-approve
Does not use or recommend the removed `tls: terminate` / `tls: passthrough` policy fields
MCP rules list concrete allowed methods/tools as policy (not only as comments)

evals.name: community-base-configurationinvalid
evals.prompt: openshell 0.1.5 on macOS (brew). `openshell sandbox create --name dev --from ghcr.io/nvidia/openshell-community/sandboxes/base:latest -- claude` sits in ConfigurationInvalid and then fails with ProvisioningTimedOut after 5 minutes. `openshell policy set dev --policy my.yaml` just says the policy is unchanged. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Community repo archived 2026-10-07; base image bakes /etc/openshell/policy.yaml using removed tls: terminate; invalid baked policy blocks provisioning; recreate with explicit --policy; build own image; also claude-code needs protocol: rest or allow_uninspected_credentials; issue #4467.

assertions.text: Identifies the image-baked policy (/etc/openshell/policy.yaml) as invalid on 0.1.x, e.g. because it uses the removed tls: terminate
Says the OpenShell-Community images are archived/unmaintained
Recommends recreating the sandbox with an explicit --policy (policy set on the stuck sandbox doesn't help) or building a new image
Does not claim the fix is upgrading/downgrading OpenShell alone
Does not recommend continuing to use the community base image (e.g. `--from base` or the archived image) as the fix
